Abstract:

This report discusses the development of physics informed Functional Link Theory of Functional Connection (FL-TFC) frameworks for solving a range of differential equations (DEs), with an emphasis on convergence, computational perfomance, and solution accuracy. The aim of the proposed approaches is to develop efficient and scalable Physics Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) frameworks that accurately incorporates the governing physical laws into the solution process. Unlike conventional PINNs, which typically rely on deep neural network architectures and penalty based formulations to enforce initial and boundary conditions, the proposed frameworks employ TFC to incorporate the prescribed constraints explicitly. To improve the representation of the solution over different computational regions, domain mapping techniques are integrated into the FL-TFC formulation. In addition, a tensor-product construction based on orthogonal polynomial bases is employed to represent solutions accuracy of DEs. These formulations provide a systematic framework for solving DEs, while maintaining high solution accuracy and favorable convergence characteristics. The effectiveness of the proposed FL-TFC based frameworks is demonstrated through benchmark linear and nonlinear ordinary and partial differential equations (ODEs and PDEs). The results show high accuracy, rapid convergence, and a compact parameterization, highlighting their potential as reliable and efficient approaches for solving DEs.
